role.altitude: The recreational therapist keeps talking with patients, families and staff, running and adapting activities and planning with the team; searching the record for restrictions, retyping interest checklists, chasing actions by mail and looking up community options shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using record summaries and assessment forms
Keeping the community resource directory current
role.ambitious_version: A therapist whose day is spent with patients, not hunting for information.

tasks.short: Read the medical record, ask staff, interview the patient, talk with family members, collect the interest questionnaire, write the assessment and follow up missing information to assess patients' capabilities, needs and interests.

steps.what: Patient or family fills in an interest questionnaire
Therapist searches medical records for diagnoses, restrictions and history
Therapist asks medical staff about the patient
Therapist interviews the patients themselves about capabilities and interests
Therapist talks with family members
Therapist writes the assessment, retyping the interest checklist
Therapist asks staff by mail for missing information

tasks.design: A summary view in the patient record shows diagnoses, mobility and fall risk, diet and activity restrictions from structured fields, instead of the therapist searching through notes. Patients or families fill an interest questionnaire on a tablet, and the answers prefill the assessment form in the record, instead of a paper checklist typed in later. Talking with staff, patients and families and writing the judgement stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Restrictions were searched in notes and checklists retyped.
tasks.enabler_now: Record summary views and tablet questionnaires feeding assessment forms.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who cannot answer questions themselves.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the hobby a patient lights up about.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and typing; conversations stay.

reach.learn: Whether fewer questions come from the therapist.

evidence.claim: Records and documentation suit integrations and forms; health data are special category data needing a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: assessing capabilities, needs and interests; developing the treatment plan (task 388) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2: restrictions and mobility held as structured fields for about 70% of patients; s2 is priced at that share.
s6 saves retyping the interest checklist; the therapist still writes the assessment.
Patients' questionnaire time is shown in s1 and replaces the paper checklist.
unknowns: Share of patients able to fill the questionnaire.
research_questions: Are assessments complete sooner after admission?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: patients unable to answer; high: patients with structured records who fill the questionnaire.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare progress summaries, attend team meetings, confer informally with members of the treatment team to plan and evaluate therapy programs, record decisions, follow up actions and check team schedules.

steps.what: Therapist prepares progress summaries for the treatment team
Therapist confers in treatment team meetings to plan and evaluate therapy programs
Therapist confers informally with nurses and other therapists
Therapist records team decisions in the record and own actions in a notebook
Therapist follows up team actions with colleagues by mail
Therapist checks team schedules and patient lists

tasks.design: Team meeting notes are a form in the patient record with action fields. Each action, with owner and date, shows in that person's worklist with a reminder, so the therapist neither keeps a separate notebook nor chases colleagues by mail. Progress summaries belong to the sibling reporting task. Meetings and informal conferring stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actions were kept in notebooks and chased by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Meeting forms with actions in staff worklists.
tasks.still_hard: Teams spread over several wards with different systems.
tasks.human_edge: Arguing in the team for an activity a patient really wants.

reach.learn: Whether actions close before the next meeting.

evidence.claim: Action lists with reminders replace notebooks and follow-up mail.

assumptions: Boundary: conferring with the team; preparing reports and charts for the team (task 396) is a sibling task.
s1 is part of preparing reports and charts for the treatment team, which sibling task 396 covers; its saving is counted there.
s4 saves keeping actions twice; s5 saves chasing by mail.
Meetings and conferring keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of team meetings per week.
research_questions: Do team actions close on time more often?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few actions per meeting; high: large teams with many actions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with patients about leisure interests, look up local options, write session notes, give information sheets, contact community organisations and follow up to counsel and encourage patients to develop leisure activities.

steps.what: Therapist counsels and encourages patients to develop leisure activities
Therapist searches for local leisure options and contacts for after discharge
Therapist writes the session note
Therapist composes an information sheet on chosen activities for the patient
Therapist contacts community organisations for the patient
Therapist follows up with the patient on new activities

tasks.design: A community resource directory, kept by the department with the municipality's social map, lists local leisure groups with contacts, accessibility and costs, filterable by interest and need. It replaces searching the web and calling around for each patient. Each directory entry prints as an information sheet. Counselling, contacting organisations for the patient and following up stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Options were searched per patient and sheets written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintained resource directories with printable entries.
tasks.still_hard: Rural areas with few accessible options.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the club where a shy patient will feel welcome.

reach.learn: Whether referrals arrive with the right information.

evidence.claim: A maintained directory with filters replaces repeated searching for the same information.

assumptions: Boundary: counselling on leisure; recording participation and progress (task 387) and discharge plans (task 20893) are sibling tasks.
s3 is part of recording participation and progress, which sibling task 387 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s2: the directory covers about 70% of patients' home areas; s2 is priced at that share.
Counselling, contacting and follow-up keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of patients discharged outside the region.
research_questions: Do more patients keep a leisure activity after discharge?

incremental.description: Therapist updates directory entries found outdated.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: patients from outside the region; high: local patients.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run activity sessions, adapt activities, prepare adapted materials, record participation, book rooms and equipment and encourage clients with special needs to acquire new skills and get involved in health-promoting leisure activities.

steps.what: Therapist runs sessions and encourages clients with special needs to get involved in leisure activities
Therapist adapts activities to each client's abilities
Therapist makes adapted instructions and materials from scratch
Therapist records each client's participation
Therapist books activity rooms and equipment by mail and phone
Therapist encourages clients between sessions

tasks.design: A shared library of adapted activity cards with easy-read text and pictograms lets the therapist start from an existing card, instead of making instructions from scratch. Activity rooms and equipment are booked in the room booking system, instead of by mail and phone. Running sessions, adapting activities, recording participation and encouraging clients stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were made from scratch and rooms booked by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared activity card libraries and room booking systems.
tasks.still_hard: Clients whose needs change from day to day.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the moment a client is ready to try something new.

evidence.claim: Shared material libraries and booking systems replace one-off materials and booking by mail.

assumptions: Boundary: encouraging skills and involvement; instructing patients in activity techniques (task 393) and recording participation and progress (task 387) are sibling tasks.
s4 is the first record of each client's participation and keeps its full time.
s3 saves remaking common materials; s5 saves booking by mail.
Sessions, adapting and encouraging keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of materials reusable across clients.

incremental.description: Therapist adds new cards to the shared library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: highly individual materials; high: reusable materials.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
